Separation of a salt into dissolved ions
Movement of electrons through a wire
Breaking a molecule by ordinary digestion

Two protons and two neutrons
One photon
One proton and one electron

A neutron pair
An electron

questions.question: What is gamma radiation?

A stream of complete atoms
Low-frequency sound
High-energy electromagnetic radiation

questions.question: What is a radioactive half-life?
choices: Time for half the undecayed nuclei in a large sample to decay on average
Time for every nucleus to decay
Time for the sample's temperature to halve
Time for every atom to lose half its protons

Only the temperature of the sample changes

questions.question: How does nuclear fission differ from fusion?

questions.question: Why is an alpha emitter potentially hazardous if taken inside the body?

It only emits harmless visible light

questions.question: Why can a radioactive tracer help study a process?

Its visible color alone measures every reaction rate

questions.question: What remains unchanged during an ordinary chemical reaction but may change in a nuclear reaction?

The identity of atomic nuclei
The number of chemical bonds

questions.question: Can the exact decay time of one particular unstable nucleus normally be predicted?
choices: Yes; every nucleus of one isotope decays at the same instant
Yes; the half-life specifies one exact decay time for each nucleus
No; decay is described using probabilities
No; so even the average behavior of large samples is unpredictable

The initial amount changes the isotope's half-life proportionally
